$comment: Descriptive, derived from the types the bounded parser reads; the parser is the only authority on validity. Where the parser reads two versions of a document with one type, this schema admits what that type admits, including members the later version adds. Byte, depth and count bounds are recorded in x-rustev-parse-limits (a string length here counts characters, the parser counts bytes), and rules applied when a plan is compiled are stated in field descriptions, not enforced here.

BatchChargeAllocation.description:
Deterministic settlement of one observed batch charge across its logical
members. Member order is the runtime-recorded batch index order.

oneOf.description:
Divide integer units evenly. Members with the lowest indices receive
one extra unit until the remainder is exhausted. The shares are
allocation evidence; the batch total is settled once, by the charge
owner, against the summed member reservations.

max_queue_delay_ms.description:
Upper bound on time a member may wait for peers. Batches are formed
within one decision's admission wave, so the runtime waits zero.

CostPolicy.description:
The cost budget of one decision, in integer units the deployment chooses
(spec 003, 3.5).

oneOf.description: Nothing is refused; charges are still recorded.

A guaranteed cap: every reachable backend must disclose an enforceable
per-call upper bound, which is reserved before dispatch.

The weaker policy: estimates are reserved, and the result is never
labeled a cap.

Delay.description: The delay before retry `n` (1-based). No jitter.

oneOf.description:
First admitted, first evicted. Cache hits do not reorder entries. A
per-scope bound evicts only that scope's oldest entries.

The monotonic clock injected into the runtime. It is process-relative,
which is sound for a memory cache that dies with the process.

FailureClass.description:
How a dispatched attempt failed (spec 003, 3.6.1). Deadline and
cancellation are not classes: they end a request, and are never retried
or a fallback trigger.

oneOf.description: The output failed the core's validation.
The adapter says the failure may not recur.
The adapter says the backend refused for load.
The adapter says the failure will recur for this input.

FallbackPolicy.description:
Runtime failure fallback (spec 003, 3.6.2), distinct from the
definition's compile-time capability fallback.

backends.description:
Backend ids tried in order after the bound backend; at most 4, none
repeated, never the bound backend.

on.description: Classes that move the request to the next backend.

MemoryCachePolicy.description:
Bounds apply to one plan's cache namespace; no plan's policy evicts
another plan's entries.

oneOf.description: Refuse when an enabled optimization cannot safely admit the request.
Execute independently without reuse and record the reason.

OptimizationPolicy.description: Plan-identified controls for reusable semantic work.

RetryPolicy.description: Retries on the same target (spec 003, 3.6.1 and 3.6.3).

max_attempts.description: Attempts per target, including the first; `1..=8`.

on.description:
Retryable classes that are retried; empty exactly when
`max_attempts` is 1.

max_attempts_per_decision.description:
Worst-case backend attempts of one decision, over every request,
retry and fallback.

optimization.description:
Optional reusable-work policy (spec 017). Its absence preserves the
version 1 policy bytes and unoptimized behavior.

steps.description:
At most one entry per semantic step; an unlisted step gets one
attempt, no timeout and no fallback.
